run.question:
Alertmanager alert PendingPodsDetected (severity critical) is firing for service otel-demo/otel-demo since 2026-11-17T09:38:33Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The PendingPodsDetected alert for namespace otel-demo is explained by an unsatisfiable node selector in the pod templates of two Deployments. Two pods are Pending in otel-demo: ad-dd7f45975-mw86p and cart-5b597c6db5-pkzkh; both report PodScheduled=False with reason Unschedulable and the scheduler message '0/5 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane: }, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector.' Both pods carry spec.nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname: invalid-node, and the five cluster nodes carry hostnames i-01a47734339426210 (control-plane, tainted), i-037e40963128cbd9f, i-0424ef08cd107882f, i-08831c4b8af18ed15 and i-097278082719f10ba, so no node matches that selector. The same value is in the pod templates of Deployments ad and cart and in no other Deployment. Events date the change: at 09:37:36Z Deployment ad scaled up new ReplicaSet ad-dd7f45975 from 0 to 1 and it created ad-dd7f45975-mw86p; at 09:37:44Z Deployment cart scaled up cart-5b597c6db5 and it created cart-5b597c6db5-pkzkh; both pods have repeated FailedScheduling events (count 3 each, last 09:47:59Z). The previous ReplicaSets ad-554b849958 and cart-755465879b have no nodeSelector, and their pods ad-554b849958-42mdm and cart-755465879b-bgb2p are Running and ready with 0 restarts on node i-037e40963128cbd9f, so the rolling update is stalled but the old pods still back the Services: Endpoints ad and cart each hold one ready address pointing at those old pods, and span-derived call rates for both services stay steady across the change point. No service-level or customer impact was observed from the two Pending pods. Two background ad error spans on flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream started around 09:06Z and 09:16Z, before the 09:37 change, and are not tied to this cause. The actor that applied the selector could not be identified because change_history is not available and admission webhooks could not be read; a metrics cross-check was also unavailable since this Prometheus holds no kube-state-metrics pod-phase series.

claims.text: Two pods in namespace otel-demo are Pending: ad-dd7f45975-mw86p and cart-5b597c6db5-pkzkh. Both have PodScheduled condition status False with reason Unschedulable and message '0/5 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane: }, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/5 nodes are available: 5 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.', node unset and no container statuses.

Both pending pods specify spec.nodeSelector {'kubernetes.io/hostname': 'invalid-node'} with the standard not-ready/unreachable NoExecute tolerations and no affinity. Pod ad-dd7f45975-mw86p requests 10m CPU / 225Mi memory (limits 50m/450Mi); pod cart-5b597c6db5-pkzkh requests 15m CPU / 55Mi memory (limits 45m/165Mi).

The cluster's five nodes are all Ready with kubernetes.io/hostname values i-01a47734339426210 (labelled node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane and carrying taint node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane:NoSchedule), i-037e40963128cbd9f, i-0424ef08cd107882f, i-08831c4b8af18ed15 and i-097278082719f10ba (all four with node-role.kubernetes.io/node and no taints). None of them carries kubernetes.io/hostname=invalid-node.

Deployments otel-demo/ad and otel-demo/cart both carry pod-template nodeSelector {'kubernetes.io/hostname': 'invalid-node'}. Cluster-wide the only other Deployments with a nodeSelector are ingress-nginx-controller, cilium-operator, coredns, coredns-autoscaler, ebs-csi-controller and opentelemetry-operator, which all use {'kubernetes.io/os': 'linux'}; no StatefulSet sets a nodeSelector.

Event timeline in otel-demo: at 09:37:36Z Deployment ad scaled ReplicaSet ad-dd7f45975 from 0 to 1 and that ReplicaSet created pod ad-dd7f45975-mw86p; at 09:37:44Z Deployment cart scaled ReplicaSet cart-5b597c6db5 from 0 to 1 and it created pod cart-5b597c6db5-pkzkh. Both pods show Warning FailedScheduling events from default-scheduler with count 3, last at 09:47:59Z, carrying the same '0/5 nodes are available ... didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' message.

The older ReplicaSets ad-554b849958 (owner Deployment ad) and cart-755465879b (owner Deployment cart) have pod-template nodeSelector null, while ad-dd7f45975 and cart-5b597c6db5 carry {'kubernetes.io/hostname': 'invalid-node'}. The old pods ad-554b849958-42mdm and cart-755465879b-bgb2p are Running, ready, restartCount 0, started 09:00:11Z and 09:00:10Z on node i-037e40963128cbd9f, while the two pending pods have startTime null.

Deployments ad and cart are each at generation 2 with observedGeneration 2, spec.replicas 1, strategy RollingUpdate with maxSurge 25% and maxUnavailable 25%, and status replicas 2, ready 1, available 1, unavailable 1, i.e. a stalled rollout keeping one unschedulable new pod alongside the old ready pod.

Service endpoints remain backed despite the stalled rollout: Endpoints ad has ready address 100.96.3.180 (targetRef ad-554b849958-42mdm, port tcp-service/8080) and Endpoints cart has 100.96.3.205 (targetRef cart-755465879b-bgb2p, port tcp-service/8080).

Span-derived call rates show no drop across the 09:37 change point: between 08:38:33Z and 09:51:33Z cart STATUS_CODE_UNSET stays roughly 15.5-20.9 spans/s and ad STATUS_CODE_UNSET roughly 0.9-2.4 spans/s, while ad STATUS_CODE_ERROR is 0 or 0.0037 spans/s at scattered points both before and after 09:37. These are span counts over every operation, not request counts.
Cluster-wide pod state contains exactly two Pending pods, both in otel-demo and both with nodeSelector {'kubernetes.io/hostname': 'invalid-node'}; no pod in any other namespace is Pending.

The ad error spans visible in the sample are two flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream spans with otel.status_code=ERROR and rpc.grpc.status_code=4, durations about 600s, started approximately 09:06:05Z and 09:16:02Z, i.e. before the 09:37:36Z Deployment change, with matching flagd child spans reporting rpc.grpc.status_code=0.

The 63 metric names returned for selector {namespace="otel-demo"} in the query window contain no kube-state-metrics pod-phase or deployment-status series; the set is container, node, process, JVM, Redis and traces based (for example traces_span_metrics_calls_total and container_memory_working_set_bytes).

Rejected: the control-plane taint alone explains the pending pods. Only node i-01a47734339426210 carries node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane:NoSchedule; the other four nodes are untainted and Ready, yet the scheduler reports those four as not matching the pod's affinity/selector because kubernetes.io/hostname=invalid-node exists on no node.

Rejected: insufficient node CPU or memory caused the unschedulable state. The scheduler message names an untolerated control-plane taint and non-matching node affinity/selector rather than insufficient resources, and the pending pods request only 10m CPU/225Mi (ad) and 15m CPU/55Mi (cart).

Rejected: the FailedScheduling and PVC provisioning events in namespace data-recorders explain this alert. They concern a different namespace and different objects (Job, StatefulSet and PersistentVolumeClaim there), pods in that namespace also show 7 Scheduled and 7 Started events, and the only Pending pods cluster-wide are the two otel-demo pods with the invalid-node selector.

The other otel-demo workloads were checked and show no pending or unavailable state: 19 Deployments besides ad and cart (accounting, checkout, currency, email, flagd, fraud-detection, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, kafka, load-generator, otel-collector, payment, postgresql, product-catalog, quote, recommendation, shipping, valkey-cart) each report replicas 1, ready 1, available 1 and condition NewReplicaSetAvailable True, with no pod-template nodeSelector.

The selector value may have been injected at admission rather than authored in the Deployment specs, since the identical literal 'invalid-node' appeared in two different Deployments 8 seconds apart (09:37:36Z and 09:37:44Z). This could not be tested because mutatingwebhookconfigurations could not be read and change_history is not integrated; the Deployment pod templates are still the objects that carry the unsatisfiable selector.

Remove the unsatisfiable nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname: invalid-node from the pod templates of Deployment otel-demo/ad and Deployment otel-demo/cart, or set it to an existing hostname such as i-037e40963128cbd9f; the Pending pods ad-dd7f45975-mw86p and cart-5b597c6db5-pkzkh would then become schedulable and the stalled rollouts could complete.

gaps: change_history is not an available integration in this Run, so who or what set nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=invalid-node on Deployments ad and cart at 09:37:36Z-09:37:44Z could not be identified.
mutatingwebhookconfigurations could not be read (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE twice), so admission-time injection of the nodeSelector cannot be confirmed or excluded.

The kube_.* metric-name query returned no data (no_data: f550c236-070c-4336-8ad6-7657f1403115-t0:66fee01d-a22b-4175-b5d9-b420bdc76174), and the metric list for {namespace="otel-demo"} shows no kube-state-metrics pod-phase series, so the pending-pod count and its onset could only be established from Kubernetes object state and events, not from metrics.

The query for the Prometheus rule named PendingPodsDetected returned no_data (12549614-5a24-4045-ba1a-e37de17ef870-t1:44a99d76-05b4-46fc-9266-e3723027b6cf), so the alerting expression and its evaluation history were not verified.

The ConfigMap scan for data containing 'invalid-node' returned no_data (ea6cd830-76f5-41f4-a610-d7ef3310c502-t1:36bb2afd-827b-4058-a2ae-7e6288bce4d3); an empty result is not evidence that no configuration source holds the value.
The StatefulSet nodeSelector query returned no_data (ea6cd830-76f5-41f4-a610-d7ef3310c502-t2:1677223c-b14d-4c0c-9524-b68852dd0ae4), so any StatefulSet-level scheduling pinning is unknown.

The resourcequota query for otel-demo returned no_data (2bdfae1a-e8eb-4091-b759-4e467cac0832-t1:a8592b70-62bb-403c-aedd-895ff17f0956); quota pressure was not examined from object state, although the scheduler message does not mention quota.

The traced-services metric-name query for kube_* returned no_data (80447cf7-139b-4d9d-b57b-23516eae1284-t0:b54f40be-da88-4d53-ad16-ce580f423de7), so Kubernetes metrics presence beyond the otel-demo label scan was not established.

The error-tagged search for service cart returned no_data (80447cf7-139b-4d9d-b57b-23516eae1284-t2:62349de9-4b5e-4407-8d8b-0ca1f96b7b95); it matches nothing, which does not prove cart had no error spans.

Error-filtered log reads of the running pods ad-554b849958-42mdm (container ad, 3952 lines read) and cart-755465879b-bgb2p (container cart, 12736 lines read) returned no_data (d0e1e1a2-4c7f-4d67-a7a4-d343d87b2c28-t2:0707c0da-6b6d-4a63-a23f-7793f09baeef and d0e1e1a2-4c7f-4d67-a7a4-d343d87b2c28-t3:3333f488-c9dc-4db6-b5f1-9e35276f6859); absence of error lines cannot be proven, and the Pending pods have no container logs because their containers never started.

Kubernetes objects were read as current state around 09:53-09:54Z, not as they were earlier in the window, so the exact moment ad and cart first became unschedulable rests on events rather than on observed object history.

The Jaeger view is a biased sample and the full-window trace search for service ad exceeded the view limit (RESULT_TOO_LARGE, total_rows 263), so ad and cart traffic was assessed through aggregate span-rate metrics rather than individual non-error spans.
next_steps: Review the audit or change history of Deployments ad and cart, and any GitOps, Helm or admission-policy source, to identify what introduced kubernetes.io/hostname: invalid-node around 09:37:36Z-09:37:44Z.
Read mutating webhook configurations once that resource is reachable to rule out admission-time injection of the selector.
After the nodeSelector is corrected, confirm the two Pending pods schedule, the rollouts reach observedGeneration==generation with unavailable=0, and the PendingPodsDetected alert clears.
Add or restore kube-state-metrics pod-phase and deployment-status series so pending-pod alerts can be validated from metrics as well as from object state.
